summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with RTOS production experience building microcontroller firmware in C++ on STM32, including interrupt-driven ISRs, FreeRTOS task synchronization with mutexes, and SPI/I2C/UART sensor drivers. Debugged full-stack embedded systems from bare-metal register programming through real-time AI/ML inference pipelines on Jetson hardware.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometer sensor drivers with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth (BLE), translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom low-level sensor driver with z-axis differential-threshold tap detection; resolved hardware sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented UART and I2C serial-protocol sensor communication with closed-loop feedback control.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in bare-metal C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture (ISRs), plus a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for inter-task synchronization and shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands (ISRs) and user override.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, Jetson+Arduino microcontroller controller over a unified WebSocket fabric.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup, 17.6→92 FPS) for real-time AI/ML inference, plus dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping via I2C mux.

Resolved 11 full-stack integration failures through rigorous testing discipline in embedded context, from hardware bring-up through field-style defects; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
